mainEntity.name: Can composite bonding make my teeth look longer if my gums are uneven?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, composite bonding can create the appearance of longer teeth by adding tooth-coloured resin material to the biting edge or sides of a tooth. This can help compensate for minor gum asymmetry by adjusting the visible proportions. However, there are limits to how much length can be added while maintaining a natural appearance. If the gum line irregularity is significant, your dentist may recommend combining bonding with other treatments such as gum contouring for a more balanced result. A clinical assessment will determine what approach is most suitable for your individual case.

mainEntity.name: How long does composite bonding last on teeth near the gum line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding typically lasts between five and ten years, depending on factors such as the location of the bonding, your oral hygiene habits, dietary choices, and whether you grind your teeth. Bonding near the gum line can be subject to different stresses compared to bonding on the biting surface. Over time, composite may chip, stain, or wear, and it may need repair or replacement. Regular dental check-ups allow your dentist to monitor the condition of your bonding and carry out any maintenance before significant issues develop.
